chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) used to say to his sons: 'O my sons! Look to the House of your Lord, so that it should not be empty of you, and so that you should not be questioned (or have conflict/second thoughts).'.

key_terms.بَيْتَ رَبِّكُمْ: The House of your Lord (referring to the Kaaba)
key_terms.فَلَا تُنَاظَرُوا: So you should not be questioned / have conflict
key_terms.لَا يَخْلُوَنَّ: So it should not be empty

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali advise his sons regarding the Kaaba?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) advises his children to ensure the Kaaba is never devoid of their presence, emphasizing the spiritual necessity of consistent devotion. The phrase 'so you are not questioned' (fala tunaẓarū) highlights the concept of accountability, where neglecting the House of God leads to divine scrutiny regarding one's fulfillment of religious duties. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that regular visitation is not merely ritualistic but a vital means of maintaining one's spiritual standing before God.
